w: Behind an unmarked black door numbered 13 in a Juarez hotel corridor, Handshake became the first Mexican bar to top the World's 50 Best list in 2024, pouring Gatsby-era cocktails under low light. Reservations vanish within minutes; its mezcal and clarified-milk punch programs draw bartenders worldwide.
s: Unmarked door 13 crowns Latin America's top bar
why: First Latin American bar ranked World's #1 Best Bar (2024), still North America's top-ranked in 2025

w: Set inside the Radisson Blu Carlton on Hviezdoslav Square, Mirror Bar won the Disaronno Highest New Entry award at the 2025 World's 50 Best Bars, debuting straight in at No. 25. Slovak produce and Habsburg-era grandeur meet in a cocktail list built around clarity, purity and local foraged spirits.
s: 2025's biggest new entry, inside a grand hotel
why: Highest new entry, World's 50 Best Bars 2025, No.25 debut, put Slovakia on the map

w: A French New Wave-styled cocktail room on Rruga Pjeter Bogdani, Nouvelle Vague debuted at No. 28 on the World's 50 Best Bars 2025, the first Albanian bar ever ranked. Black-and-white film stills and jazz set the mood for a menu leaning on Balkan produce and vintage aperitif technique.
s: Albania's first-ever World's 50 Best bar
why: First Albanian entry on World's 50 Best Bars, debuted No.28 in 2025

w: Tucked behind a nondescript Cantonese grocery shopfront in old Dongshankou, Hope & Sesame turns Lingnan ingredients, congee, herbal tonics, five-spice, into serious cocktails. A decade in, it became Guangzhou's first World's 50 Best entry in 2025, landing at No. 29 globally and No. 7 in Asia.
s: Cantonese cocktails behind a grocery-shop facade
why: Guangzhou's first-ever World's 50 Best Bars entry, No.29 in 2025

w: In a quiet corner of Shibuya, Bellwood recreates the cafe culture of late-Meiji and Taisho Japan, when East met West. Founder Atsushi Suzuki serves cocktails in a kaiseki-style course structure, sakizuke through gohan, earning No. 48 on the 2025 World's 50 Best Bars.
s: Taisho-era cafe elegance, cocktails served kaiseki-style
why: Debuted at No.48 on World's 50 Best Bars 2025

w: On the seam between Kypseli and Metaxourgeio, Line runs a zero-waste kitchen-bar hybrid, fermenting its own fruit wines, sour beers and sourdough bases in-house. It climbed to No. 8 on the World's 50 Best Bars 2025, Athens' highest-ever ranking, built on farm-direct sourcing and a refusal to throw anything away.
s: Zero-waste bar, Athens' highest-ever world ranking
why: No.8 World's 50 Best Bars 2025, Athens' best-ever placement

w: Open since 2010 on a narrow Psyri backstreet, Baba au Rum built its name on a 400-plus label rum collection and a mentorship line that seeded much of Athens' current bar scene. It remains a fixture of the World's 50 Best Bars list, No. 27 in 2025, still run by founders who trained a generation of Greek bartenders.
s: Athens rum institution, 400-plus label collection
why: Longtime World's 50 Best Bars entry, No.27 in 2025; Athens bartending mentorship hub

w: Husband-and-wife team Alonso Palomino and Gabriela Leon built Lady Bee around Peru's biodiversity, native chilies, Amazonian fruit, pisco distilled to order, moving to a new Barranco address in 2025. It won One To Watch in 2023 before climbing the World's 50 Best Bars top 20.
s: Peru's top-ranked bar, biodiversity-driven pisco cocktails
why: Peru's highest-ranked bar on World's 50 Best Bars, formerly No.13

w: Enter through a working vending machine, insert a coin and the wall slides open onto Summer Chen and Darren Lim's bar, the only Taichung venue on Asia's 50 Best. A tiny welcome Singapore Sling nods to Chen's Singapore bartending years before bottled originals are dispensed, literally, from the machines lining the room.
s: Vending-machine door, Taichung's only Asia's 50 Best bar
why: Highest-ever Taichung ranking on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025

w: A secret door inside a Cheongdam flower shop drops guests down a staircase into Alice, a curtained speakeasy running theatrical, near-molecular cocktails. Its signature Hippity Hoppity mixes vodka, elderflower and aloe vera, part of a menu that has kept Alice a regular fixture on Asia's 50 Best Bars.
s: Flower-shop trapdoor entrance in Gangnam
why: Regular Asia's 50 Best Bars entry, one of Seoul's most acclaimed speakeasies

w: Founded in 1900 and still run by the same family, Cantillon is a working lambic brewery that ferments spontaneously with wild yeast drifting in through open windows. The attached Museum of the Gueuze lets visitors watch the process before tasting bone-dry, sour, unblended lambics found nowhere else.
s: Last spontaneous-fermentation lambic brewery standing
why: Widely regarded the world's most important lambic and gueuze brewery, working museum since 1900

w: Down a flight of stairs into a centuries-old basement, Vino Underground was one of the first bars to pour Georgia's qvevri-aged natural wines for outsiders, unlabeled bottles from small growers working amber-wine methods traced back 8,000 years. It remains the reference address for the country's natural wine revival.
s: Basement pioneer of Georgian qvevri natural wine
why: Widely cited as the pioneering natural wine bar that opened Georgian wine to the world

w: Brewing continuously on Kremencova street since 1499, U Fleku claims the title of Central Europe's oldest still-operating brewery. Eight themed halls seat up to 700 for its dark 13-degree lager, Flekovsky Lezak, unavailable anywhere else, poured by waiters who still keep score with chalk marks on the beer mats.
s: Brewing continuously on the same spot since 1499
why: Central Europe's oldest continuously operating brewery, a Prague institution for over 500 years

w: An antique lamp above an unmarked laneway door is the only clue to Eau de Vie, a Prohibition-styled room that helped launch Melbourne's hidden-bar boom. Multiple Australian Bartender awards for best bar team and cocktail list later, it still runs one of the country's deepest whisky collections behind a speakeasy front.
s: Prohibition-era laneway bar, Melbourne's hidden-bar pioneer
why: Repeated winner of Australian Bartender awards; credited with sparking Melbourne's speakeasy scene

w: Descend through a working flower and wine shop on Arroyo street into Argentina's most awarded bar, opened in 2013 by Renato Tato Giovannoni. Each cocktail traces a wave of immigration into Argentina, Italian, Spanish, Indigenous, Middle Eastern, built on regional spirits like fernet, pisco and yerba mate.
s: Flower-shop trapdoor, Argentina's most awarded bar
why: Argentina's most internationally awarded cocktail bar, longtime World's 50 Best fixture

w: Set below the Cape Grace hotel on the marina's edge, Bascule pairs one of the Southern Hemisphere's largest whisky collections, over 500 labels, with harbour views and after-dark glamour. A recent refit sharpened the cocktail programme without touching the quiet, clubby mood that made it a Cape Town fixture.
s: 500-plus whiskies on a Cape Town marina
why: Long-running World's 50 Best Bars nominee, one of the Southern Hemisphere's largest whisky lists

w: Camille Fourmont's candlelit sliver of a bar near Republique helped define Paris natural wine culture from a room barely big enough for a dozen people. She pours cult growers like Jean-Pierre Robinot and Julien Courtois by the glass alongside planches of ham and cheese, no menu needed, just conversation.
s: Tiny candlelit room, Paris natural-wine cult favorite
why: Widely cited as one of the bars that defined Paris's natural wine scene

w: Facing the Christiansborg canal since 2009, Ved Stranden 10 runs no wine list and takes no reservations: guests describe what they like and staff pull a bottle from a deep, ever-changing natural and biodynamic cellar, the livelier, older sibling of Lille Bla Vinbar.
s: No list, no reservations, canal-side natural wine
why: A foundational address in Copenhagen's natural wine scene since 2009

w: A working vineyard tavern in Heiligenstadt since 1683, Mayer am Pfarrplatz is Vienna's benchmark Heuriger, pouring its own Gemischter Satz by the carafe in the same rooms where Beethoven lodged while composing his Ninth Symphony in 1817. Long communal tables and a cold buffet keep the ritual unchanged.
s: 1683 vineyard tavern where Beethoven once lodged
why: Widely cited as Vienna's benchmark Heuriger, a centuries-old wine-tavern tradition

w: Immortalised in Joyce's Ulysses, where Leopold Bloom stops for a glass of burgundy and a gorgonzola sandwich, Davy Byrnes has poured pints off Grafton Street since 1889. Bloomsday pilgrims still order Bloom's exact lunch every June 16th, in a room barely changed since the novel made it famous.
s: Leopold Bloom's Ulysses pub since 1889
why: The literary pub immortalized in Joyce's Ulysses; Bloomsday pilgrimage site

w: On the 22nd floor of a Poblado office tower, Mamba Negra pairs panoramic Medellin views with a menu splicing African, Spanish and Caribbean flavours, part of a wider cocktail renaissance that put Colombia on the World's 50 Best Bars map. Its riffs on the Negroni and mojito sit beside rum and aguardiente originals.
s: Rooftop bar fueling Medellin's cocktail renaissance
why: One of Medellin's first-ever World's 50 Best Bars entries, No.81 in 2025

w: Wall to wall in scrawled signatures and old photographs on a narrow Habana Vieja street, La Bodeguita del Medio claims to be the birthplace of the mojito, a claim Hemingway is said to have endorsed on the wall himself. The formula hasn't changed since the 1940s: rum, mint, lime, sugar, soda, muddled by hand.
s: Graffiti-covered birthplace of the mojito since the 1940s
why: Iconic historic Havana bar credited with popularising, if not inventing, the mojito

w: Behind a glass door opposite a residential security kiosk on Sukhumvit 26, Bar Us runs a multi-course cocktail menu structured like a tasting dinner, starters through savoury mains to a sweet close, riffing on pad thai, satay and black rice. It jumped 17 places to become Thailand's top-ranked bar in 2025.
s: Multi-course cocktail tasting menu, Thailand's top bar
why: Thailand's No.1-ranked bar, No.15 World's 50 Best Bars 2025

w: A speakeasy above Basant Lok market built on 1920s moonshine-era imagery, Lair broke into Asia's top ten in 2025, the first Delhi bar to do so, with a tiered menu running from easy sours to complex, spirit-forward originals. Earthy, dim-lit rooms and a pan-Asian dining floor upstairs round out India's top-rated bar.
s: India's top bar, first Delhi entry in Asia's top ten
why: Named Best Bar in India 2025, No.8 on Asia's 50 Best Bars, Delhi's highest-ever ranking

w: Hidden inside the Imperial Hotel on Hayarkon Street, Imperial Craft Cocktail Bar was the region's first to win a World's 50 Best Bars regional award, Best Bar in the Middle East and Africa in 2017, and remains the address that defined Tel Aviv's modern cocktail scene.
s: The bar that put Tel Aviv on the cocktail map
why: First Best Bar in the Middle East and Africa, World's 50 Best 2017; foundational to Tel Aviv's scene

w: A no-frills tasting room on Route 1 outside Portland pours the beers that built Maine Beer Company's cult reputation, Lunch IPA and Dinner double IPA chief among them, brewed by a company that donates a slice of every sale to charity. Bottles rarely leave New England, so the pilgrimage is the only way to drink it fresh.
s: Cult IPA brewery, Lunch and Dinner pilgrimage site
why: One of New England's most cult-followed craft breweries; Lunch and Dinner IPAs are benchmark beers

w: Down a staircase behind an unmarked door in a Gueliz apartment block, the Hadni brothers opened Morocco's first serious mixology bar in 2016. A saffron gin sour built with threads sourced from Taliouine has become the house signature, poured in a dim, intimate room built entirely around the drink rather than the scene.
s: Morocco's first mixology bar, hidden behind a plain door
why: Widely cited as Morocco's pioneering craft cocktail bar
